expected_effect: No action proposed, so no change in observables is predicted. The mechanism named by the verdict is a namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy `deny-all-recommendation` created at 10:53:18 by platform-automation [tr_87652bf6467a][tr_0c99cf700f8c]; the only effect that would clear it is removing or narrowing that policy (fix class `reconnect`), and `reconnect_service` is listed UNAVAILABLE - the executor performs only rollback_image, revert_config and restart_service. None of the three available actions meets its own preconditions here: rollback_image requires a prior image tag and a deploy/image change in the window, and the change history records no deploy and no image bump, only a first-ever workload creation [tr_87652bf6467a]; revert_config requires a prior configuration for the target service, and every recorded config event is a first creation (Service frontend, Service profile, the policy itself), so there is no earlier state to restore to [tr_87652bf6467a][tr_0c99cf700f8c]; restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and frontend's log shows a clean cold start reaching a serving state at 10:53:06 with no panic, exception or timeout afterwards [tr_d3e4bb54f84b], which points at connectivity removal, not at a wedged process. Escalate to an operator who can delete or re-scope the NetworkPolicy.
if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the policy's real selector turns out not to cover the recommendation path - one finding calls the selector metadata incomplete and says its practical effect is not established [tr_0c99cf700f8c] - in which case the fault is something else and a different action might apply. It is also wrong if recommendation's own logs (never collected) show a frozen process rather than a partitioned one, which would make restart_service on recommendation defensible. Note that the confirming signal is itself weak here: frontend has no span metrics [tr_2905d9ddfa34] and wrote no logs after 10:53:06 [tr_d3e4bb54f84b], so any remediation's success would be hard to observe on the alerted service at all - a further reason to hold.
risk: The risk of abstaining is that the partition persists and the recommendation path stays severed until a human intervenes; mean time to repair lengthens by the escalation delay. The risk of the alternative - proposing restart_service or revert_config on frontend anyway - is larger: a restart discards the serving process and its caches and would not touch the L3/L4 policy, so the outage would continue with a fresh process and a new cold-start error burst muddying the timeline; a config_revert on a service whose config was created, not modified, has no prior state and could leave it unconfigured.
blast_radius: No one sees a change, because nothing is executed. The incident's existing blast radius is unchanged: frontend (alerted seed) and the five services reached from it - profile, recommendation, reservation, search, user. The humans who notice are the on-call responders, who now carry the fix rather than this system.
